one_line: Handsfree adds voice and gesture control to WebMCP-enabled shopping sites.
what_it_does: A one-line runtime exposes existing site tools to voice and camera gesture clients without an LLM in the loop, demonstrated on a curated shop.
leverage_rationale: Structured shared tools make voice and gesture reliable clients of the site's actual actions; generic UI automation would be markedly less dependable, though the underlying shopping experience remains possible without WebMCP.
leverage_evidence: One script line and a Claude Code command wire existing frontend actions to WebMCP.
Voice, gesture, floating input, and trace panel use the same declared tools.
Frame sheet visibly shows hands-free cursor/product-panel interaction cues.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, intentionally designed shopping flow with multiple curated sections and interaction states, but no submitted video and limited visual proof of end-to-end tool execution.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and gallery contains 12 images.
Frame sheet shows hero, product rows, story blocks, and in-page product panel behavior.
Description lists concrete tools and injector verification workflow.
impact_rationale: It addresses a real accessibility and convenience desire for hands-free shopping and gives site builders a low-friction modality layer, with a clear audience even if broad utility is not established.
impact_evidence: Supports voice and camera gesture interaction for shopping.
Targets any editable website with existing frontend actions.
Curated shopping flow is visibly legible and usable.
creativity_rationale: The combination of WebMCP tool surfaces with no-LLM voice and gesture control is a fresh interaction model, pursued across a complete editorial commerce demo.
creativity_evidence: Explicitly treats the tool layer as the product and modalities as interchangeable clients.
Index-finger cursor and air-tap product/story interactions are distinctive.
Single-line integration is a memorable framing.
usability_note: Visual flow is polished and the in-page panel/hands-free cues are understandable, though gesture discoverability and robustness are not independently verified.
red_flags: No submitted video; tool invocation is primarily claimed rather than shown.
Some interaction captions are difficult to verify at frame-sheet resolution.
standouts: Shared semantic tool layer across voice, gesture, and text input.
advance_reason: Distinctive WebMCP leverage and a coherent, high-quality commerce interaction make it a strong candidate despite limited end-to-end evidence.

one_line: A buyer agent negotiates multidimensional deals with a seller agent before human confirmation.
what_it_does: A marketplace exposes search, cart, coupon, add-on, and negotiation tools so two agents can haggle price, quantity, shipping, and freebies while the human approves the final order.
leverage_rationale: The core experience—multi-round, stateful buyer/seller negotiation with constrained offers and a human confirmation boundary—depends on structured page tools and is not comparably reliable through generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Every storefront page registers search, cart, coupon, add-on, and negotiation tools.
OffersService is the single mutation path enforcing buyer budget and seller floor.
Human confirmation is enforced before purchase.
execution_rationale: The packet describes unusually complete architecture and a broad storefront, with an alive demo and multiple frame sheets showing product/negotiation packaging; exact end-to-end execution is claimed rather than video-demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Alive demo, public repository, and 95k+ product catalog are reported.
Description specifies multi-round negotiation and confirmation dialog.
Backend constraints and single transition function indicate intentional state handling.
impact_rationale: It addresses a recognizable shopping pain—negotiating complex deals—while preserving user agency and could provide credible value to bargain-oriented shoppers and sellers.
impact_evidence: Negotiates price, quantity, add-ons, shipping, and coupon stacking.
Final order requires explicit human confirmation.
Multi-vendor marketplace gives the workflow a concrete audience.
creativity_rationale: Agent-to-agent haggling over a multi-dimensional deal, rather than simple checkout automation, is novel and ambitious for a WebMCP challenge.
creativity_evidence: Buyer and store agents negotiate over several rounds.
Economic floors and budgets make negotiation substantive.
No-API-key in-page agent loop broadens the interaction concept.
usability_note: The human confirmation boundary and conventional storefront framing make the concept approachable; negotiation outcomes may still need explanation.
red_flags: No submitted video despite extensive claims.
Real catalog scale and negotiation robustness are not directly verified in the packet.
advance_reason: Transformative leverage, ambitious originality, and credible product framing warrant advancement.

one_line: Modelo combines rich-text narrative with deterministic interactive model blocks.
what_it_does: A local-first notebook lets users write prose around named numbers, sliders, selects, toggles, and formulas, save scenarios, and have an agent inspect or edit the same document.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives an agent precise access to named model state and formula dependencies in the same source-of-truth document; UI automation would be substantially more fragile for model edits.
leverage_evidence: 23 typed tools cover notebooks, models, named inputs, variables, and formulas.
Tools report changed, broken, and readability state.
BlockNote is shared as the human and tool document source of truth.
execution_rationale: The concept is coherent and technically detailed, with a clear notebook workflow and local-first architecture; frame evidence supports the interface but does not demonstrate the complete agent loop.
execution_evidence: Alive demo and public repository are reported.
Description specifies formula dependency evaluation, scenarios, and validation.
Two frame sheets show notebook/model interface states.
impact_rationale: People who build forecasts, explain models, or compare scenarios have a concrete need for narrative and deterministic calculations to coexist; agent-assisted editing directly fits that workflow.
impact_evidence: Named variables render as reactive inline chips in prose.
Scenarios support comparison of predefined values.
Agent can read and update variables and formulas.
creativity_rationale: It is a fresh, well-executed synthesis of computational notebooks, rich narrative, and agent collaboration, though inspired by an existing product category.
creativity_evidence: Narrative paragraphs and reactive model blocks are interleaved.
Agent edits preserve formula dependency semantics.
Writing tools include quality/status reporting.
usability_note: The narrative-plus-block model is intuitive for planning and explanation, with conventional editor affordances visible in the packet.
red_flags: No video; end-to-end agent collaboration is not directly shown.
Minimal version and local-only scope may leave edge cases untested.
standouts: Shared document source of truth between UI and WebMCP.
Strong deterministic semantics rather than free-form agent edits.
advance_reason: High leverage and credible execution address a real modeling workflow with a differentiated interaction model.

one_line: Threshold composes a care plan across independent organizations through one WebMCP page.
what_it_does: An assistant sends structured requirements to multiple care providers, detects incompatible links, coordinates alternatives and temporary leases, then asks the human to review and send a referral.
leverage_rationale: Cross-origin structured coordination, dependency checking, resource leasing, rollback, and privacy-preserving referral are the product; generic UI driving cannot replicate this reliably across independent sites.
leverage_evidence: Transcript shows three organizations queried concurrently through tools.
Packet demonstrates a failing arrival/admission constraint being diagnosed and repaired.
20-minute leases and release-on-failure preserve shared state across providers.
execution_rationale: The 172-second video transcript gives unusually strong end-to-end evidence: requirements, parallel search, offline handling, constraint failure, repair, lease conflict, referral review, and printable plan.
execution_evidence: Video is present with detailed transcript covering the complete workflow.
Transcript shows an offline organization withdrawn while others still answer.
Human correction and final send are visibly described as explicit boundaries.
impact_rationale: It targets a high-stakes, concrete care-coordination problem where fragmentation and time pressure cause real harm; the demonstrated solution directly composes a feasible plan while protecting privacy.
impact_evidence: Carer needs surgery while arranging dementia care, accessible transport, and home care.
System identifies the exact infeasible link and alternative.
No identifying information leaves until human referral approval.
creativity_rationale: The cross-origin care-plan composition model and explicit failure-link repair are highly original and deeply pursued, combining privacy, coordination, and resource consistency.
creativity_evidence: Independent organizations retain separate origins and state.
Plan feasibility is checked across linked services.
Assistant-mediated structured requirements avoid repeated storytelling.
usability_note: The one-story-to-one-plan flow is compelling and the printable result helps, though multi-provider coordination is inherently complex.
red_flags: Real-world provider data/integration depth is not independently established; demo scope is implied.
standouts: Privacy and cross-organization consistency are core rather than cosmetic.
advance_reason: Best packet-level combination of transformative WebMCP leverage, high impact, originality, and demonstrated workflow.

one_line: Glassmap exposes WebGL map data and actions as structured tools for agents.
what_it_does: A map makes layers, features, spatial queries, and map interactions directly accessible to agents instead of forcing screenshot interpretation.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP directly exposes structured geographic state hidden behind a WebGL canvas; agents can query features and perform spatial actions precisely where generic visual automation is unreliable.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly identifies WebGL maps as an agent black box.
Description cites structured geographic data, layers, coordinates, and spatial relationships.
Frame sheets show map-centered interface states.
execution_rationale: The product thesis and map UI are coherent, but the packet lacks video and the provided description is truncated before the concrete tool set and full workflow are evidenced.
execution_evidence: Alive demo and public repository are reported.
Three frame sheets show a consistent map product.
Description explains a concrete GIS/QA pain point.
impact_rationale: GIS developers, QA teams, and users of map applications have a real need for reliable access to features and state beyond pixels; the fit is direct.
impact_evidence: Targets debugging, development, and QA workflows involving WebGL maps.
Structured feature/layer access avoids inaccurate screenshot guessing.
GIS background grounds the intended audience.
creativity_rationale: Turning an opaque visual map into an inspectable agent surface is a strong, memorable application of WebMCP with meaningful domain depth.
creativity_evidence: Applies WebMCP to spatial relationships rather than generic page actions.
The black-box-to-glass framing captures a distinctive interaction shift.
usability_note: Map-centric UI is familiar to its target users, though agent affordances and spatial query feedback need direct observation.
red_flags: No video and truncated packet text limit verification of actual tool behavior.
Visual frame evidence alone cannot establish structured query correctness.
standouts: Clear, non-cosmetic WebMCP rationale for WebGL content.
advance_reason: High leverage and useful domain fit merit advancement, with execution confidence reduced for thin end-to-end evidence.

one_line: UNSAID lets private agents build shared agreement from minimum-disclosure signals.
what_it_does: Participants brief their own agents privately; the shared room receives structured ballots and limited signals, constructs bridge proposals, and requires human ratification.
leverage_rationale: Phase-specific tools and schema-constrained disclosure boundaries enable multi-party negotiation without exposing raw private context; a generic UI agent cannot provide comparable privacy and state guarantees.
leverage_evidence: Tools expose room state, ballots, signals, bridge proposals, and ratification by phase.
Transcript states raw private explanations never enter the room.
Tool availability changes with room state and permissions.
execution_rationale: The video transcript demonstrates a complete multi-party flow from private constraints through failed candidates, bridge proposal, unanimous acceptance, and human approval, with a clear receipt.
execution_evidence: 172-second video with detailed end-to-end transcript.
Three deterministic demo agents plus one live participant make the scenario testable.
Receipt records disclosure boundary, ballots, signals, proposal, and approval.
impact_rationale: It addresses a real and widespread coordination/privacy problem in groups making decisions with sensitive constraints, offering credible value without requiring disclosure or fixed-option polls.
impact_evidence: Examples include budget, accessibility, caregiving, and deadline constraints.
A previously impossible offsite agreement is constructed.
Human retains final decision authority.
creativity_rationale: Minimum-disclosure agents constructing a new common-ground option is genuinely novel, memorable, and pursued with a sophisticated interaction protocol.
creativity_evidence: Agents share judgments and structured signals rather than private stories.
Bridge proposal changes relevant attributes without revealing reasons.
Phase-specific permissions and ratification deepen the concept.
usability_note: The separation between private briefing and shared ratification is legible; first-time users may need explanation of structured signals.
red_flags: Three demo agents are deterministic, so fully independent multi-user behavior is not shown.
standouts: Strong evidence receipt and human ratification boundary.
advance_reason: Transformative leverage, exceptional originality, and strong demonstrated execution make it a clear advance.

one_line: Angel PT is a physical-therapy patient website with WebMCP-assisted answers, search, scheduling, and tracking.
what_it_does: Patients can ask a chatbot questions, search therapists, schedule appointments, read materials, and track activities using illustrative demo data.
leverage_rationale: The described functions are conventional website actions and chatbot interactions; no evidence shows WebMCP materially changing reliability or shared state versus ordinary browser automation.
leverage_evidence: About text lists standard search, scheduling, reading, and tracking functions.
No frame sheets or tool details were submitted.
WebMCP is named but its specific delta is not evidenced.
execution_rationale: The packet explicitly calls the app a demonstration with dummy illustrative data and no licensed clinical approval; absence of frame evidence prevents credit for complete execution.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and only one packaging screenshot exists.
About text says data/literature are not exhaustive or therapist-approved.
No submitted video or frame sheets.
impact_rationale: Patients and physical-therapy practices are a real audience, but the demo's unapproved dummy content and unspecified clinical quality limit credible impact.
impact_evidence: Targets patient questions, therapist discovery, appointments, and activity tracking.
Authors identify physical-therapy patients as users.
Content is explicitly illustrative and incomplete.
creativity_rationale: It is a conventional healthcare website with a chatbot and WebMCP additions; the packet does not show a novel interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Feature set is standard patient-portal functionality.
No distinctive WebMCP workflow is described.
usability_note: The stated feature set is familiar, but limited evidence and dummy clinical content reduce confidence in safe usability.
red_flags: Unapproved, non-exhaustive health content and dummy data.
WebMCP implementation and end-to-end behavior are unspecified.
advance_reason: Thin evidence, conventional leverage, and explicit clinical-content limitations do not support advancement.

one_line: Forge is a browser IDE where humans and agents share project development operations.
what_it_does: An open-source IDE exposes project, file, run, console, build, and deploy operations as semantic WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: Semantic tools let agents operate the development environment directly instead of using fragile clicks, keystrokes, and copy-paste; this is a substantial reliability and capability improvement.
leverage_evidence: Tools cover create/manage projects, read/write files, run, inspect console, build, and deploy.
Product is explicitly organized around agent development operations.
Frame sheets show browser IDE states and shared workspace framing.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent and the architecture aligns with the claimed workflow, but no video or direct end-to-end build/deploy proof is included.
execution_evidence: Alive demo and public repository are reported.
Two frame sheets show IDE interface states.
Description identifies a complete development lifecycle rather than code generation alone.
impact_rationale: Developers and coding agents have a concrete need for a shared environment spanning files, execution, debugging, and deployment; the product addresses a meaningful workflow gap.
impact_evidence: Targets project management, dependency/runtime operations, debugging, and deployment.
Shared human-agent project state is central to the pitch.
Open-source browser IDE broadens potential use.
creativity_rationale: An agent-native IDE is a strong and ambitious synthesis, though the category is increasingly familiar; the shared operational workspace is the fresh angle.
creativity_evidence: Moves agent interaction from chat into the actual development environment.
Exposes lifecycle operations, not only file editing.
usability_note: The IDE metaphor is familiar and shared state is valuable, but execution and deployment flows are not directly demonstrated.
red_flags: No video; central run/build/deploy workflow remains claimed.
Dependency installation and sandbox/security boundaries are not evidenced.
standouts: Treats the environment, not just code text, as agent-operable.
advance_reason: Strong dev-tool fit and meaningful WebMCP delta justify advancement, with evidence-limited execution confidence.

one_line: Ohmni gives agents structured, approval-gated access to hardware diagnostics.
what_it_does: A browser workbench connects to real or virtual ESP32 hardware so agents can inspect telemetry, run approved tests, gather evidence, request human physical changes, and retest.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP bridges agent reasoning to live hardware measurements and controlled actions with explicit safety boundaries; screenshots or generic UI automation cannot provide comparable structured telemetry and verification.
leverage_evidence: Web Serial exposes reset history, voltage, telemetry, diagnostics, and evidence collection.
Read-only tools can run autonomously; hardware-affecting actions require approval.
Physical changes are handed back to a human and verified by retest.
execution_rationale: The workflow and virtual fallback are thoughtfully scoped, but no video is submitted and frame sheets alone do not prove live serial or end-to-end diagnosis.
execution_evidence: Alive demo and public repository are reported.
Three frame sheets show diagnostic workbench states.
Description includes real hardware and deterministic virtual environment.
impact_rationale: Robotics and embedded developers have a concrete, frustrating need to turn physical telemetry into agent-usable evidence; the tool can reduce manual screenshot/log transcription while retaining safety.
impact_evidence: Targets board debugging and physical-world diagnosis.
Supports both real Web Serial hardware and accessible virtual hardware.
Safety approvals and verification address real operational risk.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP as a controlled agent-to-hardware diagnostic bridge is highly original and ambitious, especially with human-in-the-loop physical repair.
creativity_evidence: Agent reasons over measurements rather than pasted logs.
Workflow explicitly spans measurement, diagnosis, physical intervention, and verification.
Virtual ESP32 mode makes the concept demonstrable without hardware.
usability_note: The staged diagnostic workflow is credible for technical users; hardware setup and approval steps may be demanding.
red_flags: No video; live hardware behavior is not directly verified.
Physical safety and browser compatibility details are not demonstrated.
advance_reason: Novel, high-leverage hardware workflow with credible audience value merits advancement despite thin execution evidence.

one_line: Curbcut lets agents and developers inspect, propose, approve, and verify accessibility repairs.
what_it_does: A browser workbench combines editable source, isolated preview, live axe findings, exact source mapping, surgical diffs, human approval for semantic changes, and verification.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes a bounded repair protocol with shared source/preview/axe state and approval gates; generic UI driving cannot reliably preserve the same precise diff and semantic-authority boundary.
leverage_evidence: Transcript says 10 tools inspect findings, map source, preview diffs, apply repairs, and rerun axe.
Technical fixes can proceed while semantic fixes remain human-blocked.
Agent attempts to bypass approval are explicitly rejected.
execution_rationale: The video transcript demonstrates the central workflow end to end, including real axe findings, source mapping, proposal, application, verification, and blocked semantic repair.
execution_evidence: 176-second video with detailed transcript.
Tabindex finding disappears after exact repair and rescan.
Email-label proposal requires human approval and preserves untouched source until approved.
impact_rationale: Accessibility repair is a real, underserved developer need; the product reduces tedious technical work while preserving human judgment where meaning and disability context matter.
impact_evidence: Combines scanner evidence with exact source location and rendered preview.
Supports undo, export, and fresh verification scans.
Explicitly avoids overclaiming whole-page WCAG compliance.
creativity_rationale: The repair-preview-approval-verify interaction is a thoughtful and original application of WebMCP, especially the distinction between mechanical and semantic repairs.
creativity_evidence: Non-mutating proposals precede source changes.
Human approval is policy-driven by repair semantics.
Shared timeline and exact source mapping deepen the workflow.
usability_note: The three-panel workspace, diff preview, and explicit approval language make the workflow highly legible to developers.
red_flags: Static HTML/CSS scope may limit general applicability, but it is clearly stated.
standouts: Strongest evidence-backed safety and verification workflow.
Semantic versus mechanical repair distinction is excellent.
advance_reason: Demonstrated end-to-end execution, meaningful leverage, high impact, and disciplined human oversight make this a clear advance.
